answer.label: His thought — the wording changes
answer.sourceLine: Spurgeon’s 1863 sermon has “he who never quotes will never be quoted.” The circulating version substitutes “is never quoted”; the idea and speaker are supported, but the exact sentence has changed. The Spurgeon Library sermon ↗

source.excerpt: He who never quotes will never be quoted.
trail: Spurgeon’s 1863 sermon has “he who never quotes will never be quoted.” The circulating version substitutes “is never quoted”; the idea and speaker are supported, but the exact sentence has changed. The Spurgeon Library sermon ↗

The Spurgeon Library provides the sermon text and its date, 29 November 1863. Quote Investigator independently traces the maxim to the same sermon and shows later versions. Read the supporting source ↗

author.name: Charles Haddon Spurgeon
author.heading: About Charles Spurgeon
author.bio: Charles Spurgeon delivered this sermon at the Metropolitan Tabernacle. His advice about reading and quotation forms part of an argument that even preachers should learn from other people’s books.
